survey: A spiral-clipped topiary shrub in a round stone planter ring on a lawn. The foliage forms one helix that winds upward in four turns, getting narrower toward the top, and ends in a small rounded crown. Each turn rests on the one below it and slopes the same way, so the spiral reads as continuous. The bottom turn sits on a brown soil bed inside the planter ring, and a soil edge shows all the way around, so the shrub is grounded and not floating. The planter ring is a low ellipse made of stone segments. It sits flat on the grass and is seen at a shallow three-quarter angle. Its width matches the angle, so it is a plausible circle in perspective. The tools found no thin parts, loose ends or branches. No trunk shows between the turns. That is an acceptable simplification for a dense, stylized topiary.
